companyDescription: Rare-disease biopharma — PYRUKYND/AQVESME (mitapivat) is the only approved pyruvate-kinase activator for hemolytic anemias, now filed for sickle cell disease
summary: REFRESH (prior report Sep 29, 2026). Mitapivat's SCD PDUFA lands Nov 1 (priority review); the stock is +7.6% since Sep 29. Consensus moved to $45.88 (+21.4%), so it just clears the 20% gate (BofA $50, Truist cut to $37). Q3 earnings follow Nov 5. fda_decision is n=3 in core feedback (context only). Written against the core Base optimism bias of +23.7pp (realized 14d P75 +6.6%, P90 +11.7%). Base +15% assumes approval and a ~1-month re-rating toward $43. catalysts.name: Mitapivat sickle cell disease sNDA — PDUFA (priority review)
catalysts.description: FDA goal date Nov 1, 2026 (a Sunday — action could land Oct 30 or Nov 2). Approval would make mitapivat the first PK activator for SCD.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 earnings
catalysts.description: First read on SCD launch readiness and PYRUKYND thalassemia uptake.

risks: Approval is not certain: Agios discontinued tebapivat in SCD (Jul 2026) after Phase 2 failed to show a differentiated profile — SCD has been a hard indication.
Consensus upside is only ~21% — much of an approval may already be priced after the run from $22.
Launch execution in SCD (payer access, physician adoption) against established therapies.
Sunday PDUFA date — the action may arrive a day early or late.
Label risk: a narrow label or safety monitoring requirement would cap sales.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds at 3.75-4.00% after the surprise Sep 16, 2026 hike (first since 2023). The Oct 27-28 FOMC is priced ~93% hold / ~7% +25bp as of Oct 25 — but hike odds briefly spiked to ~44% after the hot Sep CPI print on Oct 14, so the path stays two-sided.
macroRisk.inflationNote: September CPI +0.6% m/m, 3.7% y/y headline; core +0.3% m/m, 2.6% y/y — both above consensus. Headline re-acceleration keeps a further 2026 hike live.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Commercial-stage rare-disease biotech with ~$2.3B cap; rate sensitivity is moderate, the FDA outcome dominates.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — the Oct 28 FOMC is priced ~93% hold, but September CPI ran hot (3.7% headline) and a further 2026 hike is still live. October's growth/AI-infra selloff was largely a rates trade, so the decision and the dot path matter directly for this name's multiple.

entryStrategy.verdict: BUY (Speculative) — a priority-review PDUFA 6 days out with modest (~21%) consensus upside. The measured core median at-catalyst return is -6.9% with 74% of picks underwater at their event (n=54), so Entry 2 ($34.50-36) is preferred and Entry 1 is a starter only.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Priority-review PDUFA names typically see a modest drift into the decision date as positioning builds, though moves 40-200%+ in either direction are common on the day itself given how binary the outcome is

postWin.note: Agios's own precedent: AQVESME thalassemia approval (Dec 23, 2025) moved AGIO +19.97% same day (open $24.85, close $29.50). Sector context: small-cap priority-review approvals typically run +30-100%+, though a well-anticipated approval on an already-large-cap name can be muted — see Madrigal's +11% on the first-ever MASH approval (Mar 2024), where much of the move was pre-priced.

postLose.note: Industry-wide priority-review CRL pattern: 'fixable' (CMC/procedural) CRLs average -15% to -35%; 'fatal' (efficacy/safety) CRLs average -40% to -80%. No direct Agios CRL precedent exists for mitapivat — this is a category-level reference, not a company-specific case.

spotSizing.reason: 5%. fda_decision has n=3 in core feedback (context only). Approval odds are reasonable, but the tebapivat SCD discontinuation (Jul 2026) shows the indication isn't easy; consensus upside is only ~21%.
